First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }-\frac{5}{3}\cdot {(\frac{2}{7})}^{x} & =(-\frac{5}{3})\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the graph of $y={(\frac{2}{7})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943873/assets/9a249437f97a441c409b17e0f30a59bdcb70df02610f18d9320361d3d0d6708a.png)

From the graph, we see that the function decreases to zero as $x$ increases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x}=0.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(-\frac{5}{3})\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x}=(-\frac{5}{3})\cdot 0=0.
$$
